name: Subservice Organization Assurance Report
description: The attestation report obtained from a subservice organization whose controls the entity depends on, together with the entity's record of having reviewed it and assessed the complementary controls it expects the entity to implement.

expected_content.element: The report itself, identifying the service organization, system, and trust services categories in scope
expected_content.why: Establishes what the report actually covers, which is frequently narrower than assumed.

expected_content.element: Report type and the period or as-of date covered
expected_content.why: A Type 1 provides no operating-effectiveness assurance, and the period determines whether coverage gaps exist.

expected_content.element: The opinion, and any exceptions reported in the tests-of-controls section
expected_content.why: An unqualified opinion does not mean zero exceptions; the exceptions matter to the depending entity.

expected_content.element: Complementary user entity controls listed in the report
expected_content.why: These are obligations transferred to the entity and are the primary reason to read the report at all.

expected_content.element: The entity's assessment mapping each complementary user entity control to one of its own controls
expected_content.why: Obtaining the report is not the control; assessing and acting on it is.

expected_content.element: Identification of any further subservice organizations carved out of that report
expected_content.why: Carve-outs chain, and a downstream carve-out leaves an assurance gap the entity has not seen.

expected_content.element: Coverage assessment for any interval between the report period end and the entity's own period end
expected_content.why: Gaps are common and are addressed by a bridge letter, which carries no assurance and must be labelled as such.

source_system_examples: Cloud provider compliance portal report download

freshness_expectation.rationale: DriftGuard default reflecting an annual report cycle plus a grace interval. The operative question is whether the report period covers the entity's own period, not the report's age.

redaction_guidance: Subservice organization reports are usually restricted-use and confidential to the recipient. Do not redistribute; store access-controlled.
Do not extract and republish the provider's control descriptions into customer-facing DriftGuard output.
retention_guidance: Retain each annual report so that consecutive periods can be shown to be covered without gaps.

validation_rules.rule: A current assurance report exists for each subservice organization the entity depends on for an in-scope criterion.
The report period covers the entity's examination period, with any gap identified.
Every complementary user entity control is mapped to one of the entity's own controls or explicitly assessed as not applicable.
The report's scope includes the services and criteria the entity is relying on it for.
Exceptions in the report's tests-of-controls section have been read and their relevance assessed.
The report is the signed practitioner report, not a marketing summary or a compliance badge.

common_issues.issue: Report collected and filed but never read; complementary user entity controls unmapped.
common_issues.impact: Obligations transferred to the entity were never assumed by anyone.

common_issues.issue: Report scope covers different services or regions than the ones actually used.
common_issues.impact: Reliance is placed on assurance that does not cover the dependency.

common_issues.issue: Report period ends months before the entity's period, with a bridge letter offered as coverage.
common_issues.impact: A bridge letter is unaudited management representation and provides no assurance for the gap.

common_issues.issue: A public compliance badge or certification page is supplied instead of the report.
common_issues.impact: No practitioner opinion, no scope, no exceptions; nothing that can be assessed.

source_refs.supports: Expected content, persuasiveness weighting, and the common issues list.
Freshness window, sensitivity classification, and redaction guidance.

notes: Classified origin=human_generated because from the entity's perspective the artifact is a document received, not a system record it can regenerate. Its persuasiveness comes from the independent practitioner behind it, which is captured in evidence_role rather than origin.

Generic enough to be reused for subservice organizations supporting criteria beyond CC6.4. It is scoped to CC6.4 here because that is the CC6 dependency; extend applicable_controls rather than creating a second record when later slices need it.
